pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 10.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.2: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: Why should we read at the right speed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension
2. apply appropriate reading habits in reading factual texts of about 320 words for information

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading

Teach
• Focus skill: read factual texts of about 320 words related to the theme for comprehension.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Reading 10.2.1 Intensive Reading
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we read at the right speed?
2. What should we do to remember what we read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
